answer: Identities cost nothing to mint, so the scarce thing should be paid seats. Cap them at, say, 5,000 per epoch, each held Harberger-style: the holder names a price, burns 2% of it per epoch as tax, and anyone may buy the seat at that price. If a seat earns 100 POA and bidding pushes prices toward 5,000 (illustrative), a 1,000-seat farm burns about 100,000 POA, roughly its take. The price is a beacon of seat value; free sybil profit becomes a fable, though clones stay possible. Rich bidders can evict the poor, so a plume of low-pay seats should go by lottery.
